# ValidateSchema

Validates a value against a JSON Schema and lists every failure.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
ValidateSchema(data, schema)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | any | The value to validate: any value that can be written as JSON, null included. A function value, a value that contains itself, nesting deeper than the limit, or a string with an unpaired surrogate is a runtime error, as for `ToJson`. |
| `schema` | object | The schema, an object. Null, or any other type, is a runtime error; boolean subschemas `true` and `false` are accepted inside it. |

## Returns

Array. An array of failures, empty when data is valid. Each failure is an object of `path`, the JSON Pointer of the value that failed (the empty string for data itself, and for `required` and `dependentRequired` the location of the absent property), `keyword`, the keyword that failed, and `message`, the keyword followed by `" at "` and the path, or `"(root)"` for the empty path. `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not` and `contains` each give one failure at the value, without the failures of their subschemas; `propertyNames` gives one failure at each property whose name fails; `if` is never reported, only the failures of `then` or `else`. The failures are sorted by path and then by keyword, comparing code unit by code unit, and each pair of path and keyword appears once. Never null.

## Remarks

The schema is read as JSON Schema draft 2020-12, limited to these keywords: `type`, `enum`, `const`, `multipleOf`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `minimum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `maxItems`, `minItems`, `uniqueItems`, `prefixItems`, `items`, `contains`, `maxProperties`, `minProperties`, `required`, `dependentRequired`, `properties`, `patternProperties`, `additionalProperties`, `propertyNames`, `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not`, `if`, `then`, `else`, `$ref` and `$defs`, together with `$schema`, `$id`, `$anchor`, `$comment`, `title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`, `deprecated`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly` and `format`, which are accepted and have no effect on the result.
 The whole schema is checked before the value is, whatever the value is. A runtime error is raised for a keyword not in that list, for a keyword whose value has the wrong form for draft 2020-12, for a `$ref` that is not a local reference starting with `#` or that does not name an object or a boolean in the schema, for a chain of `$ref`, `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not`, `if`, `then` or `else` steps that comes back to where it started, and for a `pattern` or `patternProperties` key that is not a valid regular expression.
 The type `"integer"` accepts every number whose value is whole, `5.0` included. `maxLength` and `minLength` count UTF-16 code units. A `pattern` matches when it is found anywhere in the string, with the same regular expressions as the regex functions. `enum`, `const` and `uniqueItems` compare values as the `==` operator does.

## Example

`ValidateSchema({ "age": "ten" }, { "type": "object", "properties": { "age": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": ["name"] })` returns `[{ "path": "/age", "keyword": "type", "message": "type at /age" }, { "path": "/name", "keyword": "required", "message": "required at /name" }]`.
